mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of instances when UNRATE increases > 0.5pp.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 declines for 2 consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth expectations improve.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances when INDPRO increases > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of instances when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% over two months signals a strengthening demand for housing, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates broader economic growth.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances when HOUST increases > 5% over 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 2% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure despite accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 2% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS < 2% and CPIAUCSL increases > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in retail sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as it indicates a broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when RSAFS declines for 2 consecutive months.
